scope: Official comparator evidence for conductivity-limited soil-water routing; no native or manuscript edits.

units.tau: dimensionless; first-day fraction of above-FC water lost from initially saturated soil

manual_facts.claim: Tau is a drainage fraction, not a time constant.

manual_facts.domain: theta_fc < theta <= theta_sat; r=0 for theta<=theta_fc
manual_facts.sign: r is a positive decrease in stored water content.

manual_facts.claim: Thickness converts content loss to released water depth.
Incoming drainage accumulates with local release; restricted transmission fills the receiving and upstream compartments. Cumulative flux cannot exceed the receiving layer conductivity.
Net controlled irrigation bypasses rainfall curve-number runoff. Topsoil Ksat limits admission; deeper limits cause storage and backup. Excess becomes runoff unless retained by bunds.
Bund height sets finite surface storage; retained water persists for infiltration or evaporation. Initial surface water can be specified.
Default compartments are 0.1 m. The infiltration algorithm retains compartment-thickness dependence; complete grid invariance is not claimed.
Ksat describes saturated horizon transmission. Water-retention values apply to fine soil; gravel reduces water-holding volume and is assumed nonconductive.

input_file_units.SAT,FC,PWP: vol.% in official soil file; divide by100 for equations
input_file_units.gravel: mass.% in soil file, converted to volume.% internally

official_code_facts.algebraic_consequence: Before remaining-capacity capping, drain_max = InfRate * r_threshold/r_sat; at saturated threshold it equals InfRate. Thickness and gravel factors cancel.
official_code_facts.classification: algebraic consequence of pinned official code, not an observed measurement

official_code_facts.claim: Profile-rejected infiltration is returned to finite bund storage when bund height is at least 0.01 m; overtopping remains runoff.

diagnostic_inference.classification: source-backed structural inference; native code not reviewed by this source-audit task
diagnostic_inference.claim: A thin-layer local storage-release cap imposed on all incoming irrigation omits the separate conductivity-scaled transmission mechanism. Changing a fixed fraction to tau alone does not address that omission.
diagnostic_inference.numerical_context: For hypothetical FC=0.30 and SAT=0.45 m3/m3, a saturated 0.05 m compartment releases 3.26–6.04 mm/day under FAO tau at Ksat100–586mm/day, whereas its saturated infiltration capacity is Ksat.
diagnostic_inference.native_option_relationship: The native conductivity-scaled reservoir cascade is a distinct engineered mechanism. These sources do not establish an AquaCrop implementation or replication.
physical_constraints: Preserve water mass and conductivity bottlenecks in every layer.
Finite surface storage requires a justified bund-height or depression-storage assumption.
Conductivity-scaled throughflow does not justify unconditional infiltration.

illustrations.classification: hypothetical analytical calculations; neither observations nor native model results
illustrations.input_origin: Ksat range supplied by parent; theta/dz selected for illustration
illustrations.old_fraction_origin: Parent-reported legacy0.6perday; native implementation not independently inspected.

limitations: No source establishes the correct SoilGrids Ksat for a particular field.
The manual empirical drainage function is not a Richards-equation solver.
Storage release and infiltration transmission use different factors in official code.
Only named source routines and equations were reviewed; official program was not executed.
Public manual cover and title pages identify7.3July2026 despite isolated inconsistent contents-page footers.
Independent field-response validation remains separate from mechanism and mass-balance checks.
